summary: The selected result is a machine-checked example for an explicitly published open question of Grünbaum (Math. Intelligencer 2010), case k = 10, which he described as having no information. It sits in discrete geometry, in the theory of parallelohedra, tilings and zonohedra, and specialists in nonconvex parallelohedra and rhombic monohedra (the Grünbaum, Senechal–Taylor line of work) are a clearly identifiable audience. The literature account quotes the question and the related remarks accurately. It finds and credits earlier web-published solids of the same family (Hall 2016, Inchbald, Kostick 2022) and claims no priority for a k = 10 example, only for the proof and for the witness. Two sources are disclosed precisely as not read or unverifiable: a closed-access 2023 paper, of which only the abstract was read, and private correspondence. Neither is used for priority. The independent search found no omission that changes the public account.

internal_notes.message: Notability basis: this gives a rigorous example for a case of a named open question in a well-known expository research paper by a leading discrete geometer, and the example also refutes a tentative remark in that paper. The audience is specialists in tilings, parallelohedra and zonohedra, and in mathematical crystallography (Senechal–Taylor). The result is narrow in scope: one witness, a known family, and k ≥ 12 left open. It plausibly supports a serious research note but does not reach beyond specialists. The calibration theorems are sanity checks for the zone definition and are rightly grouped with the main result rather than scored on their own.

Earlier solids of the same family were shown as space-fillers on the web, but without proof and without any link to Grünbaum's question. The submission states this plainly and does not claim the first k = 10 example. Novelty is not required, and the submission's contribution (the first proof and the explicit link to the question) is accurately framed. Whether Hall's solid has all zones of size 10 was not checked independently. The submission does not depend on it, because it claims only GET B.

Minor slip: the submission says Kostick's page has no reference to zones, but the page says 'a set of 3 parallel zones indicated as blue bands'. This is a passing use of the word, not zone counts and not Grünbaum's question, so it does not change the public account. It should be corrected to 'mentions zones but not zone sizes or Grünbaum'.

An earlier Kostick page (2 Jan 2022) is not cited. It shows an array of triacontahedra dimpled in or out on 3-face groups in octahedral symmetry, and a single triacontahedron dimpled in tetrahedral symmetry. No translation tiling by one cell is claimed on the page. It does not displace GET B or the 2016 Hall date, but it is worth adding for completeness.

Evidence limit: closed access, and only the abstract could be read here too. Their three nonconvex parallelohedra come from skeletons of Fedorov's convex parallelohedra, so they are unlikely to be rhombic monohedral with zones of 10. Which Grünbaum statement they counter could not be confirmed, and it may be the same tentative indentation remark. The submission discloses this precisely and claims no priority from it, so it is not a finding. The private correspondence is disclosed as unverifiable and used for nothing.

No Lean, Isabelle or other formalization of parallelohedra or zonohedra was found in the searches. The submission's negative search report is plausible, and an independent search of Mathlib was not repeated here.
These are cited but not read, and the submission says so. The convex belt-size fact (4 or 6) is standard and correctly stated.

what_would_reach_higher: Obtain and read Senechal–Taylor 2023, through an institutional library, interlibrary loan or a request to the authors for a copy. Then state exactly which Grünbaum statement they counter, and whether any of their three solids is rhombic monohedral or has zones larger than 6. This closes the one gap that could change the account.

Correct the Kostick description: the 2022 page mentions zones (as 'blue bands') but gives no zone sizes and does not mention Grünbaum. Also cite the 2 Jan 2022 Kostick page with tetrahedrally and octahedrally dimpled triacontahedra.

Make the priority picture checkable: for the Hall/Inchbald solid and Kostick's GET A cell, give the zone sizes (are all six zones of size 10?) as a stated computation, so readers can see whether the earlier web solids already answered k = 10 informally, not just that they are space-fillers.
Read Williams, Natural Structure p.196, or a free scan or library copy of it, and state whether the eightfold indentation shown there tiles or has 10-face zones.

Raise notability: extend the Lean development to GET A and the Hall/Inchbald solid, with a formal non-congruence proof. Better still, give a classification of all indentations of the triacontahedron that are parallelohedra, or address k ≥ 12. Either would turn one witness into a structural result.
Publish the computational study, as a preprint or a short note in a discrete-geometry venue, so that the result and its context can be cited and inspected outside the repository.
